text:
Maria: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a single, minimal "actor" shape for service tokens so policy checks are deterministic. Thoughts on adding a project_affinity field?
Devon: +1 on a single actor shape. project_affinity sounds useful but we should be explicit about semantics: is it an assertion or an authorization hint?
Jia: I'd treat project_affinity as authoritative when present on customer-managed keys, but as a hint for org-level tokens. Means: customer keys pin to a project, org keys don't.
Sanjay: That matches my mental model. One place this bites: proxies that actuate on behalf of another svc — we need a proxied_by or chain array. Otherwise logs and RBAC are wrong.
Ash: Agreed. Proposal: actor := { kind: "service" | "user" | "job", id: string, project: string? }, plus optional proxied_by: [actor]. Simple and flat.
Maria: Example token payload: ```json
{
  "actor": { "kind": "service", "id": "svc-cache-01", "project": "payments" },
  "issued_at": 1689000000,
  "exp": 1689003600
}
```
Devon: That's clear. Two enforcement rules to decide: 1) If actor.project present, only allow resources scoped to that project unless caller holds cross-project privilege. 2) If absent, require org-level RBAC check.
Jia: We should also prevent actor.id collisions across projects. If svc-cache-01 exists in two projects, the authoritative identifier should be "project/id" or we canonicalize to "projects/{proj}/svcs/{id}" internally.
Sanjay: +1 canonicalization. Implementation detail: our authn layer can accept legacy flat ids but normalize them at ingress. Add a warning header for clients.
Ash: How do we handle delegation? Example: infra-proxy (org-level) calls billing-svc (project-scoped) to do a constrained action. We need a proxied_by chain and a policy evaluation mode (stop-on-first-deny vs cumulative).
Maria: I prefer stop-on-first-deny with an allowlist on proxies. Policy engine should see chain: [ {proxy org svc}, {original actor} ] and evaluate from leaf to root, respecting the most-restrictive effective scope unless a proxy has explicit "can-act-on-behalf-of" capability.
Devon: Edge-case: long proxied chains might blow logs and cache keys. Limit chain depth to 3 and drop older entries with a truncated flag.
Jia: Also consider token minting: ephemeral tokens minted by proxy should carry both original_actor and minting_actor to prove intent. Example mint payload: ```json
{
  "actor": { "kind": "service", "id": "svc-proxy-1", "project": "infra" },
  "on_behalf_of": { "kind": "service", "id": "svc-analytics-2", "project": "billing" },
  "scope": ["read:secrets"],
  "exp": 1689000300
}
```
Sanjay: Sounds good. For audits, we must persist both fields as separate columns so queries like "who acted in billing in last 7 days" remain simple.
Ash: Migration plan: 1) accept both legacy api_key (flat) and new actor tokens at ingress for 3 months; 2) normalize and emit deprecation header; 3) after window, reject ambiguous flat ids.
Maria: Security check: make sure KMS/HSM keys used for customer-managed tokens include project metadata so a leaked key can't be used across projects.
Devon: Ops note: caching layer needs to key on normalized actor + proxied_by hash + token expiry to avoid privilege leakage when tokens are rotated.
Jia: Can we add a tiny RFC snippet to the repo with these shapes + enforcement rules? I'll draft it after this thread.
Maria: Perfect. Action items: Jia draft RFC snippet, Ash and Devon draft normalization + ingress changes, Sanjay add audit schema change. I'll create a follow-up thread for the migration schedule. :thumbsup:
